subject: Critical Thinking
title: Daniel Kahneman: Two Systems of Thinking
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Daniel Kahneman: Two Systems of Thinking.

hook.text: A psychologist won the Nobel Prize in Economics.

buildup.text: With Amos Tversky, Kahneman discovered that human thinking uses two systems: fast, intuitive System 1 & slow.

discovery.text: System 1 makes 95% of decisions: automatic, effortless, & often wrong.

twist.text: We THINK we're using System 2. We're usually using System 1. The illusion of rationality is the deepest bias.

climax.text: 'Thinking, Fast and Slow' became the bible of behavioral economics, nudge theory, and modern decision science.

punchline.text: You think you're thinking. Most of the time, you're just reacting.

quiz.question: What are Kahneman's two systems of thinking?

details.summary: Daniel Kahneman's research revealed that human decision making relies on two systems: fast, intuitive System 1 and slow, deliberate System 2. His work with Amos Tversky demonstrated that cognitive biases are systematic and predictable.
details.whyItMatters: Kahneman's framework gives you a practical model for understanding when to trust your intuition and when to engage deliberate analysis.
takeaways: System 1 is fast and automatic but prone to biases
System 2 is slow and effortful but more accurate
Kahneman and Tversky identified dozens of systematic biases

faq.question: What was Kahneman and Tversky's most important contribution to critical thinking?
faq.answer: They proved that human irrationality is not random but systematic and predictable. This meant biases could be studied scientifically and potentially counteracted through structured decision processes.

faq.question: How did Kahneman's work change economics and public policy?
faq.answer: It spawned behavioral economics, which replaced the assumption of rational actors with a more realistic model of biased decision makers. This led to policy innovations like default opt-ins for retirement savings and organ donation.
